summary.headline: ECOS Q2 FY27 revenue INR2,345 mn (+9.5% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 11.9% and PAT +21.4% YoY to INR177 mn.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR2,345 million, up 9.5% YoY and 10.9% QoQ, with H1 revenue of INR4,458 million (+12.8% YoY). EBITDA rose to INR279 million (11.9% margin) from INR218 million (10.3%) in Q1, driven by lower cost of service (74.2% of revenue vs 75.1%) and lower employee cost as a share of revenue. Management reiterated 13-15% revenue growth for FY27 and a INR1,000 crore revenue aspiration by FY28, while guiding H2 EBITDA margin to 10-11%. Management said it walked away from business below its pricing threshold, and the balance sheet remains debt-free with working capital (receivables at 46 days) a watch item.

financial_highlights.change: +13.8% YoY; +27.9% QoQ (Q1 margin 10.3%, Q2 FY26 margin 11.5%)
Isha Jain question cited H1 EBITDA growth of 7.3% YoY
+7.8% YoY; down from 11.2% of revenue in Q1

vs INR61.55 million in Q1 FY27

segments.name: Employee Transport Services (ETS)
segments.commentary: 58% of Q2 revenue; management described ETS as lower-margin than CCR, with demand steady from IT, ITES and GCCs. Segment EBITDA not disclosed.

segments.name: Chauffeur-driven car rentals (CCR)
segments.commentary: 42% of Q2 revenue, share up slightly QoQ on corporate demand. Management said CCR carries a slightly higher margin; segment EBITDA not disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 13% to 15% over FY26.
Aspiration to reach INR1,000 crore revenue by FY28; management said the path depends on conversion of opportunities into business.
EBITDA margin guided at about 10%, within a 10% to 11% range, average over the next two quarters (H2 FY27); Hem Upadhyay earlier cited 11% to 13%, which Rajesh Loomba corrected.
Vehicle capex planned at INR35 crore to INR45 crore; own vehicles to stay at 5% to 10% of total fleet.
ETS and CCR revenue mix expected to stay steady, moving by only 1-2 percentage points quarter to quarter.
Employee productivity gains from AI to flow into FY28 headcount planning rather than immediate cuts.
capex_capacity: Fleet of about 20,500 owned and vendor-operated vehicles at 30 Sep 2026, up about 12% YoY; roughly 95% from vendor partners.
EV fleet increased to 475 vehicles from 460 at end of Q1; management is taking a measured approach to EV scale-up.
Footprint of 160 cities in India after adding nine cities in the quarter.
H1 FY27 capex of INR273.90 million, mostly vehicles; FY27-28 vehicle capex guided at INR35 crore to INR45 crore.
Vehicle supply is added in line with demand rather than ahead of it, per management.
demand_pricing: Trips: about 1.58 million in Q2, up 15% YoY and about 7% QoQ; H1 trips crossed 3 million, up about 21% YoY.
Clients: 72 new clients onboarded in Q2 (vs 67 in Q2 FY26 and 61 in Q1); active base of 1,538 enterprise clients, up about 10% QoQ.
Around 50% of revenue from clients associated with ECOS for more than five years.
Pricing: management let go of new business below its internal pricing threshold; said competitors in large ETS contracts are bidding at losses for top-line growth.
Margin pressure attributed to ETS mix shift over 2-3 years and competitor pricing pressure over the last 1-1.5 years.
Event and wedding/conference business is a small but fast-growing share, handled by a dedicated team set up 1.5 years ago.
Management said average ticket size has shrunk, so revenue has grown more slowly than trip volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other current assets rise from INR75 crore to INR126 crore, and is it mainly unbilled revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Hem Upadhyay said about INR24-25 crore reflects mutual fund redemption proceeds settled T+2 and booked as other current assets per auditor advice. The rest is mostly unbilled revenue, which he said is close to INR100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why has EBITDA margin fallen from around 15% to 11-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Loomba cited a shift in mix from CCR to lower-margin ETS over 2-3 years, plus competitor pricing pressure over the last 1-1.5 years that compressed gross margins.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be expected going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected the earlier range to 10-11%, with around 10% as the confident number; H2 is expected in the same range, with no sharp step-up.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and cash decline: how is working capital managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables are steady at 46 days of revenue, same as March 2026; a delayed billing issue at one or two clients has been resolved. CFO said cash and equivalents are around INR122 crore now (INR137 crore in March), with the decline linked to vehicle purchases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and own-vehicle share?
qa_highlights.answer: Vehicle capex of INR35-45 crore planned, covering economy, luxury and EV vehicles. Own vehicles to stay at 5-10% of fleet to keep the model asset-light.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI adoption progressing and what does it do to headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: AI work started 3-4 months ago with 8-10 projects; a new Microsoft Dynamics ERP went live last month. Benefits are expected to feed into FY28 manpower planning; management said net employee count has not risen much in the last six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on vendor supply as competition squeezes fleet owners?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects competitive pricing to create unsustainable last-mile economics, reducing supply investment and eventually forcing clients to pay true costs. It said ECOS has lost some RFPs by holding its price floor.

risks_watch: Competitive pricing in large ETS contracts; ECOS has lost some RFPs by holding price thresholds.
Working capital: receivables at 46 days and unbilled revenue rising to about INR100 crore; management flagged collections as a H2 focus.
Margin guidance (10-11%) sits below the H1 level of 11.2%; the earlier 11-13% range was corrected on the call, so the guidance is not yet consistent.
Vendor fleet supply: vendors under pricing pressure may slow fleet additions, as Pranay Agrawal raised; management did not quantify this.
Revenue growth lagging trip growth because of lower ticket size; FY27 growth guidance of 13-15% against H1 growth of 12.8%.
Segment profitability is not disclosed; the ETS and CCR margin split was not provided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, customer retention and the margin discipline, but the tone was cautious on pricing, with management repeatedly saying it would not chase low-margin business. Management corrected its own margin range mid-call, and several answers to balance-sheet questions were given loosely and deferred to the CFO.
key_quotes: we strategically let go of certain new prospective business that was lesser than the pricing threshold that we have decided upon, as we don't think it's prudent to grow the business at the cost of our margins.
Our approach has always been to build supply in line with the requirements of the business rather than build capacity ahead of demand.
we would continue to remain asset light. We would continue to ensure that our own vehicles stay in the range of 5% to 10% of our total fleet

adds.what: Vehicle capex of INR35-45 crore over next 2 years (own vehicles 5-10% of fleet); fleet ~20,500 owned and vendor-operated vehicles at 30 Sep 2026

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 13-15% (midpoint 14%), cut from prior 18-20%, backed by trip volume growth (~15% YoY in Q2, H1 trips +21%) and 72 new clients, with vehicle capex of INR35-45 crore and a fleet of ~20,500 vehicles, though no hard order book figures were given.

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 9.5% YoY while trips rose about 15% YoY and new clients rose to 72 from 67, so growth is volume-led and organic; ticket size shrinkage is slowing revenue relative to trips, and no one-off items were disclosed for the quarter.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided H2 FY27 EBITDA margin to about 10% (10-11% range) versus 11.9% in Q2 and 11.2% in H1, citing ETS mix shift and competitor pricing pressure.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Vehicle capex of INR35-45 crore planned over next 2 years, but vehicle supply is added in line with demand, fleet ~20,500 vehicles up ~12% YoY, so no hard new-capacity date was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Trips about 1.58 million in Q2 (+15% YoY) and H1 trips +21% YoY, with 72 new clients in Q2 and active base of 1,538 clients, though revenue growth lags trips due to lower ticket size.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Vehicle capex of INR35-45 crore guided over next 2 years, with H1 FY27 capex of INR273.90 million already spent; this is a plan rather than a new capacity announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance was cut to 13-15% from 18-20%, H1 growth is 12.8%, and margin guidance was corrected down to about 10%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue growth of 12.8% sits below the 13-15% FY27 guide, and management is walking away from low-margin RFPs and losing some bids, so the revenue guide is at risk.

rows.label: Walking away from below-threshold pricing
rows.why: Management let go of business below its pricing threshold and lost some RFPs; competitors bid at losses in large ETS contracts, so pricing discipline is likely to cap top-line growth while supporting margins.

rows.label: Receivables and unbilled revenue watch
rows.why: Receivables at 46 days (INR1,114.56 million) and unbilled revenue near INR100 million; management flagged collections as an H2 focus, so working capital could tie up more cash.

rows.label: AI-driven productivity into FY28 headcount
rows.why: AI projects (8-10) started 3-4 months ago and a new ERP went live; employee cost fell to ~10% of revenue from 11.2% in Q1, but benefits are expected to feed FY28 manpower planning rather than immediate cuts.

tone.note: Management was confident on trip volumes, client retention and margin discipline, but cautious on pricing and corrected its own margin range mid-call; analysts pushed on the margin fall from about 15%, the working capital and cash decline, and whether the 13-15% revenue guide holds.
